towns.name: Nairobi
towns.description: Kenya's capital and largest city. Hub of the matatu network.

towns.name: Mombasa
towns.description: Kenya's second city and coastal hub. Matatu routes connect the island to mainland areas.

towns.name: Kisumu
towns.description: Lakeside city in Western Kenya. Matatu routes radiate from the CBD Bus Park.

towns.name: Nakuru
towns.description: Rift Valley's largest city. Routes connect Railways & Ziwani termini to residential estates.

towns.name: Eldoret
towns.description: North Rift commercial hub. Routes serve Langas, Huruma, Annex, and university campuses.

towns.name: Thika
towns.description: Industrial town north of Nairobi. Routes serve Makongeni, Landless, Gatuanyaga, and Section 9.

notes: Route numbers: Nairobi uses NTSA numbers. Regional towns use city-prefix prefixes: Mombasa (M-), Kisumu (K-), Nakuru (NK-), Eldoret (EL-), Thika (TK-).
Fares shown are typical ranges — they vary by time of day (peak hours are more expensive), weather, and demand.
Operating hours are approximate. Most routes start early morning and end by 8–10 PM.
SACCO names reflect official registered transport SACCOs operating along these corridors (e.g. 2TS in Thika, 4NTE/Nakuru Line in Nakuru, Kitwek in Eldoret).
Stage coordinates are mapped to actual geographic coordinates of local stages and land marks across each town.
Data verified against public transportation records, NTSA SACCO registries, and local commuter reports.
source: NTSA Registered Transport SACCOs & Public Commuter Route Registry
